newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag to up return on energy sales to 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Viag to up return on energy sales to 20 pct.

text.p: German diversified utility group Viag AG said on Tuesday it was targeting a 20 percent return on sales and a 10 percent return on capital employed (ROC) in its energy business by the year 2000.
Viag Chairman Georg Obermeier told shareholders at the group's annual meeting that Viag would seek a 10 percent return on sales and a 12 percent ROC in its chemicals business.

Obermeier said Viag was seeking a six percent return on sales and a 12 percent ROC in its packaging business and returns of two percent on packaging sales and six percent ROC in its logistics unit in the same period.
Obermeier went on to detail start-up losses in its telecommunications joint-venture, which would reach between 3.6 and 3.7 billion marks by 2001.
Viag would pick up around 45 percent of these costs, with the remainder falling to its telecoms partners British Telecom and Telenor. The telecoms business should become profitable in the year 2001.

Obermeier said that had the group used the International Accounting Standard (IAS) accountancy method to work out its figures for 1996, Viag's group net profit would have been around 200 million marks higher than the 1.06 billion marks reported.
Viag reported its figures according to German accounting law. The group would have benefited by around 200 million marks from tax write-offs had it used the IAS system, Obermeier said.
